title: SATB2 · Four separate follow-up analyses

composition.headline: Four of 16 proportion models pass sampling checks; two relative mixed-cluster associations need cautious interpretation.
findings: The same frozen Scanpy and Seurat nuclei were tested in four populations, each in the full cohort (6 WT and 6 cKO) and the separate shared-partition cohort (6 WT and 3 cKO). Raw mouse counts and proportion plots are retained.

The strict same-model sampling check qualifies four models: both excitatory shared-partition models, Scanpy inhibitory shared-partition, and Seurat inhibitory full-cohort. The other 12 models remain inferentially inconclusive.

At native expected Bayesian FDR 0.05, Scanpy excitatory C9 has coefficient 0.48499, PIP 0.99333 and native compositional log2 fold change 0.64668; Seurat excitatory C4 has coefficient 0.46792, PIP 0.99596 and compositional log2 fold change 0.62512. Both are shared-partition, reference-relative associations in clusters labeled mixed atlas subclasses.

The selected mixed-cluster labels cover largely the same nuclei: shared-partition overlap is 3,197 of 3,284 in the union (Jaccard 0.9735); across all 12 mice it is 4,264 of 4,391 (Jaccard 0.9711). This is measured computational membership agreement, not a new fit or independent biological replication.
The two numerically qualified inhibitory models have no credible coefficients under this specified model. This does not establish equivalence or absence of biological effects.

The initial 0.90-target sampler family remains preserved with 0 of 16 diagnostic passes. The globally specified stricter sampler check changes numerical sampling only; biological inputs, references, model, seeds, FDR and quality rules are unchanged.
limitations: Twelve of 16 models still fail sampling diagnostics. In particular, no accepted broad-population or CA1-program composition inference follows from those failed models; inconclusive results are not negative biological findings.

Excitatory reference clusters Scanpy C14 and Seurat C21 carry saved immune/glial-associated signature-review flags. Positive relative coefficients in mixed C9/C4 do not establish expansion of a named stable neuronal cell type or absolute tissue abundance.

The tools reuse the same mice and nuclei. Strong measured membership agreement does not resolve the mixed clusters’ biological subtype, establish a named stable cell type or provide independent replication; the reference and sampling caveats still apply.
Genotype partly overlaps sequencing partition; the shared-partition cohort has only three cKO mice. The full and shared cohorts are separate exploratory analyses, not independent replication.
Posterior inclusion probability and expected Bayesian FDR are not frequentist gene-DE p-values. Each model has its own native family; uncertain labels and reference dependence remain.
composition.archive_note: Download both SATB2_composition_initial_20261028_v1.zip and SATB2_composition_strict_20261028_v1.zip from the release. Both complete native sampler families are preserved, including inconclusive models; the initial family is not additional biological replication.

cellchat.headline: Strict DEG-only CellChat retains three exploratory lower-cKO full-cohort associations; primary partition sensitivity remains inconclusive.
findings: Six molecular pairs across nine source–target contexts pass the original matching-endpoint Seurat DESeq2 rule: every required ligand and receptor complex subunit has padj<0.05. Original component up/down directions remain in the tables.

Primary triMean full-cohort associations are lower Slit1–Robo1 from deep-associated CA1 to inhibitory C6, and lower Tenm3–Adgrl2 from C6 to both deep- and superficial-associated CA1 programs; each full-cohort BH value is 0.0064935.

The primary shared-partition BH value is 0.0714286 for each of those three contexts; none of nine primary shared-partition tests passes 0.05. Both averaging methods retain the three full-cohort score directions.

The prespecified truncated-mean sensitivity yields seven full-cohort and five shared-partition associations. It is a separate sensitivity family and does not independently confirm the primary results.

Readable corrected dot, tile, circos, circle and mouse-boxplot PDFs/PNGs are available. They preserve exact saved values/scales and fix display margins, headers and vertical jitter only; archival originals remain explicitly labeled.
limitations: Both-end DEG selection reuses the same study before score testing. The score associations are exploratory post-selection evidence, with partial genotype/technical-partition confounding.
Each retained pathway context contains only one qualifying pair here, so LR and pathway test results duplicate the same evidence. The combined direction view is not an additional test family.
No qualifying strict-DEG edge for C8 does not mean absence of communication; C8 identity uncertainty remains. The DEG restriction intentionally omits most possible signaling.
RNA-based scores do not establish protein binding, physical communication, pathway activation, synaptic transmission, functional E/I balance or anatomical deep/superficial layers.

Circos sector/ribbon geometry is relative within each condition; compare saved score tables rather than interpreting cross-condition absolute ribbon thickness. Circle plots retain their saved common edge scale.
cellchat.archive_note: Complete original scientific objects, exact tables and separate corrected-layout provenance are included in this verified native archive. Corrected figures are the readable default; archival figures retain known display issues.

monocle3.headline: Four molecular state graphs and gene-module analyses completed; biological temporal direction is not established.
findings: CA1 DL/SL programs: 20,456 nuclei, 10,618 tested features, two components, 9,056 graph-associated genes and 47 modules. The smaller component contains 847 nuclei, is mostly superficial-associated and includes all 12 mice.

Separate inhibitory models retain C1: 1,718 nuclei, 3,669 graph-associated genes and 19 modules; C6: 501 nuclei, 1,439 genes and 8 modules; C8: 468 nuclei, 2,002 genes and 11 modules. Every scope contains all 12 mice.
All selected graph-associated genes had native successful tests, PCA-loading coverage and module assignments. Complete gene tables and raw module aggregates accompany the figures.
Primary graphs are unrooted. Optional native orderings use genotype-blind arbitrary references, with alternative-reference distances preserved; changing references materially changes rankings.

Module heatmaps use display z scores of mouse/endpoint aggregates, not genotype fold changes. Native gene-overlay colors are each gene’s percentage of its own maximum, not detection fraction or a shared absolute scale.
limitations: A mature P60 single snapshot supplies no independent temporal root. These are exploratory expression-state graphs, not a biological clock, WT-to-cKO progression or demonstrated deep-to-superficial transition.

Native graph_test is a same-data cell-level autocorrelation screen with a separate BH family per model. It is not an independent-mouse genotype-DE test; original DESeq2 fits remain the genotype gene evidence.

Genotype/program structure and partly confounded sequencing partition remain contributors to geometry. Same-partition files are filtered views of the same graph, not refits; coverage of all 12 mice is not formal topology stability.

Mitochondrial- and astroglial-associated module patterns require quality/background interpretation before a neuronal mechanism is claimed. Native module numbers do not correspond to hdWGCNA module IDs.
Inhibitory identities were modeled separately. No CA1-to-interneuron or C1-to-C6-to-C8 lineage was forced, and C8’s mixed identity is not resolved by learning a graph.
monocle3.archive_note: Complete native unrooted CDSs, reference-ordering objects, nearest-neighbor indexes and all gene/module tables are included in this verified native archive. Graph distance has no established biological temporal direction.

velocity.headline: Input blocked: no scVelo fit, velocity map or latent-time analysis has run.
findings: The inspected current study objects contain ordinary RNA counts, not genuine separate spliced/unspliced layers. Intron-inclusive gene counts cannot substitute for those measurements.
Historical records describe 11 LiSC BAMs; current cKO_933 read-level inputs remain unverified and inspection of the existing LiSC connection returned access denied.
No sample was silently omitted and no synthetic velocity layers, arrows or latent times were generated. The saved input assessment and blocked review explain the exact evidence gap.
limitations: Restore the existing LiSC connection, then verify all 12 matching BAM/indexes, corrected barcode/UMI tags and the matching GTF/reference, especially cKO_933, before an additive counting plan.
No velocity or latent-time conclusion follows from expression UMAPs or Monocle state distance. Mature-neuron kinetics may remain weak or unidentifiable even after valid counting.
No scientific velocity results or model archive exists for this blocked task. This section must remain unavailable until authentic splicing inputs and a separately reviewed analysis are available.
velocity.archive_note: There is no velocity-result archive. Only the verified input assessment and blocked-analysis review are provided.

root_approval_note: Root reviewed actual terminal results, native and independent reviews, status/limitations and exact four native archive remote digests. This permits fresh offline presentation build only. Public release, complete offline ZIP and live online delivery remain separately gated.
